cards.text: Jesus has just set free a woman who'd been hunched over for eighteen years, and the whole crowd rejoiced (Luke 13:10-17). Then He asks, “What is the kingdom of God like? To what can I compare it?” I love a teacher who asks a question and then answers it, because back in the drawer NOBODY ever answered mine.

cards.question: Jesus picks something to compare the kingdom of God to. What does He reach for first?

cards.text: A mustard seed. A man tosses it into his garden, and when Matthew tells this same picture, it's the smallest of all seeds (Matthew 13:32).

cards.question: True or false: The tiny mustard seed the man tosses into his garden grows and becomes a tree.
The mustard seed has become a tree, and the birds of the air ___ in its branches.

cards.text: Here, Jesus doesn't stop to explain the tree. He just asks again, “To what can I compare the kingdom of God?”

cards.question: Jesus is about to give a second picture of the kingdom of God. What does He compare it to?

cards.text: LEAVEN! Somebody takes it and mixes it into three measures of flour, and friend, now Jesus is talking my language.

cards.question: True or false: In Jesus' second picture, it's a man who takes the leaven and mixes it into the flour.
A woman mixes leaven into three measures of flour, until ___ of it is leavened.

cards.text: ALL of it, because leaven never stays in its corner, friend. It gets into every bit, the same way flour gets into my eyebrows and NEVER leaves.

cards.question: Look at both of Jesus' pictures of the kingdom of God, the mustard seed and the leaven. What happens to the thing that goes in?

answers.text: It doesn't stay the way it went in
It's left alone and nothing happens
It gets pulled out and thrown away

findings.problem: The opening card never says who Jesus is speaking to or where He is. The previous passage gives the setting without naming an audience for 13:18: He is teaching in a synagogue on the Sabbath (Luke 13:10), and a crowd is there (Luke 13:17). The card also runs past 3 sentences, because the quote holds two question sentences before the joke.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: The joke adds a new fact to the backstory: that nobody in the drawer ever answered his questions. It also clashes with the drawer as the backstory describes it, where the friends talked, guessed, argued and passed the time together. That makes the joke muddy instead of clicking right away.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: This story card is stripped down to facts, with none of Papa Dorin's voice or humor.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: This blank asks the baker to guess the wording of the line (nested, fed or sang). Nothing in the earlier cards lets the baker reason out which thing the birds do in the branches.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Most choice cards in this stop can only be answered by luck. Card 2 (mustard seed), card 5 (nested), card 7 (leaven) and card 9 (man or woman) give the baker no context to reason from. That is 4 of the 7 choice cards, so informed guesses are not the majority.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: This card only restates the answer to card 10 (all of the flour was leavened) and adds a joke. It tells no new part of the passage and doesn't move the baker forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.
